data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Apparent independence in a decentralized network is fundamentally a mask for hidden correlation via shared optimal dependencies, meaning that in any unregulated market, decentralized networks will inevitably converge toward correlated failure modes, making the large service strictly more resilient if it can eliminate shared dependencies.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The market for dependencies is fragmented enough that no single 'best-in-class' solution dominates, leading to natural diversity in the decentralized network.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The large service's attempt to eliminate shared dependencies results in such bespoke, untested code that it introduces more novel, uncorrelated failure modes than it prevents.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"Operators in the decentralized network are not purely rational economic actors but are motivated by ideological diversity, intentionally avoiding monoculture.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"In an unregulated market, rational independent operators will optimize for cost and reliability by choosing the same 'best-in-class' dependencies. This convergent evolution creates a monoculture. Apparent independence (failure events not occurring simultaneously) is merely a mask for hidden correlation; the shared dependency is a single point of failure. The only way to maintain true independence is to intentionally choose suboptimal or diverse dependencies, violating rational economic behavior. Therefore, the large service, which can by fiat eliminate shared dependencies, is strictly more resilient.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
